content:
Maria (CS): FYI flagged by AcmePay. They say answers got much worse after last night’s rollout. Customer says short factual answers are now hallucinating extra steps. They think we flipped some ‘draft’ behavior on the model.

acme_support_bot: [autogenerated] Ticket #AP-4321 opened at 1768504300 by Acme Pay. Severity: P2.

Maria (CS): Repro notes attached by customer: prompt + model output before/after. They asked for rollback if this is a known change. Raising here to get a quick triage. @Peyton @Sam can you confirm whether speculative/draft decoding was part of the rollout?

Peyton (Eng-ML): Looking. I can repro locally with the customer prompt. Notably, the new model binary had draft_generation enabled by default for some routes — that would allow the runtime to emit partial candidates and re-rank which can change answer shape.

Peyton (Eng-ML): Customer repro (using their sanitized prompt):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"acme-q2-2026","prompt":"How do I reconcile chargebacks for international cards? Provide step-by-step guidance.","max_tokens":250,"temperature":0.0}'
```

Peyton (Eng-ML): With model acme-q2-2026@v3 (pre-rollout) we get short factual list of steps. After rollout (acme-q2-2026@v4 with draft_enabled=true) output includes speculative paragraphs about unlikely legal steps and invented internal APIs. Sample diff (abridged):

Before: "1) Pull transaction logs. 2) Match transactions to invoices. 3) Contact bank..."
After: "1) Pull transaction logs. 2) Cross-check with the Acme Payment Gateway API (acme_gateway.lookup) to validate... 3) Draft a formal dispute using the standard dispute template..."

Sam (Eng-Runtime): That matches a flag we pushed in the rollout config: route config 'enable_draft_generation: true' for the "assistant-classic" family to improve latencies by allowing earlier emits + speculative re-ranking. It was intended for low-temp creative workloads. Looks like it leaked onto customer-facing billing routes due to a routing mismatch.

Sam (Eng-Runtime): Deploy details: rollout 1768501200 -> traffic split 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 hours. We expected only canary traffic but an environment selector mismatch caused 100% on some tenant routes.

Iman (Product): Oof. That explains the content shift. Product note: draft generation can change surface-level phrasing and may introduce extraneous assumptions. We should treat it as a behavior change and notify customers.

Maria (CS): Customer specifically: "We used to get concise compliance-safe steps. Now the model invents internal endpoints and recommends unsupported workflows. This is risky." They want either rollback or a mitigation toggle they can set per-tenant.

Peyton (Eng-ML): Actionable triage: 1) Reproduce with exact model id & tenant. I have local repro for acme-pay tenant header. 2) If route config exposed draft flag, rollback that flag for affected model version immediately. 3) If rollback not possible fast, provide customer with pinned model version (v3) to keep behavior stable. 4) Longer-term: disallow draft flag on any model used for compliance/ops prompts by default.

Sam (Eng-Runtime): I can stage a rollback for the routing flag now. Rolling back to previous routing config will stop draft emission in ~30s for new requests. But traffic already processed may have changed customer data.

deploy-bot: Deploy rollback job queued (#rb-176850-1). ETA 00:00:45 to start.

Maria (CS): Please confirm the command I can give the customer to pin v3 so they can test while we rollback: they use our standard header approach.

Peyton (Eng-ML): Tell them to set model param to "acme-q2-2026@v3" explicitly in the API call. Example:
```
{"model":"acme-q2-2026@v3","prompt":"...","temperature":0}
```

Peyton (Eng-ML): Also ask for one more failing prompt that reproduced hallucinated internal APIs — that will help write a unit test to prevent regressions.

Iman (Product): I'll prepare a customer-facing note once we confirm rollback. Should include root cause (routing flag leak), mitigation (pin model / rollback), and ETA for postmortem.

Sam (Eng-Runtime): Rollback started. Observability: I'm watching p95 latency and model emission logs. If draft flag goes away, we should see re-ranker calls drop in traces.

deploy-bot: Rollback job #rb-176850-1 started at 1768504520.

Peyton (Eng-ML): Confirming on my end: test call with tenant header shows outputs back to pre-rollout shape. Sending diff to Maria for customer evidence.

Maria (CS): Sent customer update: "We rolled back a routing flag that enabled an experimental draft generation mode on your model. Please test pinned v3 and confirm if issues are resolved."

acme_support_bot: Customer response at 1768504700: "Thanks — behavior looks better with v3 pinned. Please share postmortem and prevent this for our billing endpoints."

Iman (Product): We'll schedule a postmortem and add a product guard to block draft flags on sensitive route tags. Assigning follow-ups: Peyton (write regression tests & monitor), Sam (change rollout selector to be tenant-aware), Iman (customer comms & product guard), Maria (confirm customer satisfied).

Peyton (Eng-ML): I'll add an automated eval comparing v3->v4 on a curated prompt set; if output divergence > threshold we block the rollout.

Sam (Eng-Runtime): I'll add a runtime check that prevents 'enable_draft_generation' from applying when route.metadata.sensitivity == "compliance".

Maria (CS): Customer has confirmed fix. Closing on my side after we post the PM. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
